title: Light Switch: back-to-back toggle performance is degraded compared to previous versions

judgment.rationale: The exact five-second broadcast timeouts and shared UI/CLI symptom make blocking theme notification a focused hypothesis, not proof of a particular recipient or thread blockage. Use the complete supplied setup for maintainer reproduction; asking the reporter to repeat elevation tests or provide the existing settings screenshot would be redundant.
evidence: The screenshot shows Schedule Off, System theme enabled, Apps disabled, and no light/dark PowerDisplay profiles selected.
The author reports the first toggle is immediate, the next stalls about five seconds, and additional toggles queue; changing CLI theme also hangs, while setting the already-current state does not.
Both elevated and non-elevated operation were already compared; neither changes the behavior.

Source inspected at main 9227a8497750: src/modules/LightSwitch/LightSwitchLib/ThemeHelper.cpp: Successful theme writes synchronously broadcast WM_SETTINGCHANGE/WM_THEMECHANGED with 5000-ms SendMessageTimeoutW bounds, plus a system-light colorization broadcast. https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/9227a8497750c257a0682b53c556d07f48ed8ff3/src/modules/LightSwitch/LightSwitchLib/ThemeHelper.cpp
Visually inspected the supplied configuration image and compared the current helper with its CLI-change history (#50459). No covering performance fix appeared in the bounded PR search.
No report ZIP is supplied, but a controlled toggle/broadcast timing comparison can discriminate the hypothesis without blocking triage on a generic diagnostic request.
judgment.recommended_action: Time rapid toggles against theme-notification waits

fix_assessment.rationale: Qualified lightweight investigation/fix direction, not a full design. The precise five-second constant and no-op versus write distinction are corroborating source evidence; no measured broadcast or thread trace proves the blocking branch yet.

proposed_fixes.title: Bound theme-notification work without queuing stale toggles
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: synchronous broadcast waits on the state-changing path serialize subsequent toggles and CLI completion; the observed duration matches a configured timeout, but recipient/thread timing is not captured.
plan: Measure write-versus-notification latency under the reported System-only configuration and attribute the first long wait.
If confirmed, separate/bound notification delivery while preserving required shell/app refresh and orderly state ownership.
Define burst semantics so superseded state changes do not accumulate; retain immediate no-op handling and report only confirmed applied state.
verification: Back-to-back UI and CLI toggles do not wait for a full hung-recipient timeout on the command/UI path.
The shell updates correctly, already-current commands remain fast, and rapid sequences settle to the intended final theme.

reproduce.title: Time rapid toggles against theme-notification waits
reproduce.version_requirement: 0.102.2933 versus current stable/main; compare 0.100.x only in an isolated baseline.
prerequisites: Use an isolated test account or controlled test machine; preserve existing user data.
steps: 1. Set Schedule Off, apply theme to System only, leave Apps and both PowerDisplay profile options off.
2. Toggle twice rapidly from the UI/hotkey and record state changes and completion times; repeat with a short burst.
3. Compare CLI set-to-current, set-to-opposite, and toggle commands under the same setup.
4. In a maintainer diagnostic build/session, time registry writes and each notification separately; repeat with normal recipients and a controlled unresponsive theme-message recipient.
reproduce.expected_result: Theme state changes and command completion remain bounded and responsive; input bursts do not leave an obsolete queue of theme writes.
